name: client-login-webgpu-hero-20260612
goal: Ship a clean Halo Fire secure client login page using the official Halo Fire logo, Apple Liquid Glass-inspired UI treatment, and a live Three.js halo/flame hero that is reference-gated, visually inspected, and free of fake data or internal client-facing text.
exit_criteria: The visible page is the secure login surface, not a marketing page, dashboard, modal teaser, or fake-data screen.
The hero is a live Three.js canvas scene using an extruded logo-derived flame mesh, one animated halo ring, and sparse ember particles.
The hero does not use a pasted flame image, visible texture rectangle, hero card, implementation label, or hidden draggable logo as the primary visual.
Pointer drag tugs/stretch-pulls the 3D flame material and does not rotate the entire display.
The official Halo Fire logo remains deterministic in the header and login card and all logo images are non-draggable.
The login page copy is concise, client-grade, and contains no fake metrics, demo credentials, permit/AHJ overclaims, internal-alpha wording, web-scraping copy, or co-development explanation text.
Layout uses recorded composition math: golden-ratio desktop split, stable safe zones, no clipping, and responsive mobile constraints.
Visible controls use Apple Liquid Glass-inspired materials with dimensional buttons, glass inputs, focus/hover/pressed states, and readable contrast.
A real Codex in-app browser preview screenshot is saved, decoded, visually inspected, and marked pass/reject.
Focused tests, production build, loop guard, and workspace rulebook verification pass before commit.
verification_gates: Focused tests: npx vitest run tests/client-login-static.test.js tests/workbench-deep-link.test.js tests/consolidate-surfaces.test.js
Browser preview: Codex in-app browser at localhost shows rendererMode webgpu when WebGPU is available, heroReady true, fallback opacity 0, and no console errors
Interaction smoke: drag over #haloHeroScene records released after dragging and images remain draggable=false
Formal proof posture: NO_FORMALIZABLE_CLAIM for visual-only HTML/CSS/Three.js rendering and copy changes
